newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Orogen names Chevron as gas agent.
newsitem.headline: Orogen names Chevron as gas agent.

text.p: Orogen Minerals Ltd said on Thursday it has named Chevron Corp's Chevron South Pacific Ltd as its agent to market its 15.75 percent share of gas from the Kutubu onshore field in Papua New Guinea to north and central Queensland.
The gas is earmarked to be transported via a proposed 2,400 km pipeline estimated to cost A$3 billion.

In addition, Orogen said it has joined with Chevron and several other licensees to the Kutubu PDL-2 license in forming a consortium to seek expressions of interest from international pipeline companies for the development, construction and operation of the pipeline.
The other licensees include The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, Mobil Corp, Oil Search Ltd, Petroleum Resources Kutubu Pty Ltd, a landowner group, and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd.
The pipeline is planned to extend from Kopi in Gulf Province, PNG, to north and central Queensland.
Orogen, the PNG government's listed investment arm for resource projects, said the consortium's objective will be to commence deliveries of gas to north and central Queensland by 2001.
"It is expected that the 20 percent interest which Orogen currently holds will be diluted once a pipeline company joins the consortium," Orogen said.
"Although the project is still in early stages, it is a very exciting development for Orogen," Orogen managing director Charles Lepani said in a statement.
John Powell, project manager for the pipeline, said on Wednesday talks were in advanced stages with industrial gas consumers in the port cities of Townsville and Gladstone over taking gas.
